## What happens when an org owner downgrades their plan

**Authorization.** The downgrade is submitted through the `changePlanAction` Server Action in `src/actions/billing/change-plan.ts`. Its `run` handler (built via `withAction(changePlanSchema, handler, ...)`) first validates the payload against `changePlanSchema` in `src/schemas/billing.ts`, then calls `can(actor, "org:manage_billing", { kind: "billing", orgId })` from `src/lib/permissions.ts`. `can()` consults `ROLE_MATRIX["org:manage_billing"] = "owner"`, so only a user with the `owner` role passes; anyone else gets a `ForbiddenActionError`. As a second, belt-and-suspenders check, `billing-service.ts`'s `changePlan()` re-runs `assertOrgScope` and `assertCan` before doing anything else, since that service can also be invoked outside the Server Action.

**Comparison before acceptance.** Before the downgrade is allowed, the current usage is compared against the target plan's limits — twice. In the action itself, `assertPlanFitsCurrentUsage` (lines 49-67 of `change-plan.ts`) pulls `getUsage(actor, orgId)` from `src/server/services/usage-service.ts` and `getPlanLimits(input.plan)` from `src/config/plan-limits.ts`, then for `seats`, `projects`, and `storageMb` calls `wouldExceedLimit(plan, resource, used, 0)` — essentially "does existing usage already exceed the smaller plan's caps?" If so it throws `PlanLimitError` and the change is rejected before any write happens. `billing-service.ts`'s `changePlan()` repeats the same check (plus `webhooks`) as a safeguard.

**Where the plan is recorded.** The authoritative value is the `plan` column on the `subscriptions` table (`src/server/db/schema/billing.ts`), written by `subscriptionRepo.updateSubscriptionPlan(orgId, plan, interval)` in `src/server/repositories/subscription-repository.ts`, which also resets `status` to `"active"` and bumps `updatedAt`. There's also a denormalized `plan` column on `organizations` (`src/server/db/schema/organizations.ts`), intended purely as a display convenience — `billing-service.ts` explicitly documents that the subscription row is authoritative and every quota decision should read it via `planFor(orgId)`. Notably, `changePlan()` never writes `organizations.plan`; nothing in the codebase resyncs it after a plan change.

**Downstream consequences.** After persisting, `changePlan()` emits `billing.plan_changed` (`src/lib/event-bus.ts`) with `from`/`to` plan values. Two subscribers react: `activity-service.ts` records an audit-log entry, and `webhook-service.ts` enqueues an outbound webhook delivery (later sent by `src/server/jobs/webhook-delivery-job.ts`). Back in the action, `revalidateTagged([orgTag(orgId)], CACHE_PROFILES.hours)` invalidates Next.js cache tags so pages refetch. A separate `trial-expiry-job.ts` cron can independently trigger the same downgrade path when a trial ends.

**Where the new plan changes behavior outside billing pages.** Feature gating: `isEnabled()` in `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` uses `planAtLeast(ctx.plan, strategy.minPlan)` to gate flags, and `snapshotFlags()` feeds the dashboard layout so UI features (e.g., kanban, CSV export) immediately reflect the new plan. Resource-creation limits: `src/actions/projects/create-project.ts` and `src/actions/members/invite-member.ts` fetch `getOrganizationSummary()` (which reads `organizations.plan` via `organization-service.ts`'s `findOrgById`) and block creation once usage hits `getPlanLimits()` caps; `create-webhook.ts` and `create-issue.ts` follow the same pattern for webhooks and issues-per-project.

The one consistency risk worth flagging: `create-project.ts`, `invite-member.ts`, and similar action-level checks read the denormalized `organizations.plan`, not the authoritative `subscriptions.plan`. Since `changePlan()` only updates the `subscriptions` row and nothing syncs `organizations.plan` afterward, those enforcement points can keep acting on the pre-downgrade plan value indefinitely, while `checkLimit`/`planFor` in `billing-service.ts` (which correctly prefer the subscription row) see the new plan right away.
